contentBlocks.text: This week you built a complete kinematic toolkit — from a precise definition of motion to equations that solve real motion problems. Let's put it all together.

Quick review: distance is the total scalar path length; displacement is the vector net change in position (Day 1). Average velocity is displacement divided by time, v=Δx/Δt (Day 2). Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, a=Δv/Δt (Day 3). For constant acceleration, v=v₀+at finds final velocity and d=v₀t+½at² finds displacement (Day 4). An object starts at v₀=6 m/s with acceleration 5 m/s² over 4 seconds. Find its final velocity and displacement, then explain in your own words how displacement, velocity, and acceleration are all connected.

Excellent work this week — you can now describe and calculate motion precisely, the essential foundation for the forces unit ahead, since Newton's laws describe exactly what causes the acceleration you calculated this week.

objectives: Apply the kinematic equations to a new constant-acceleration scenario
Explain how displacement, velocity, and acceleration are conceptually connected
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child solve the v0=6, a=5, t=4 problem independently.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet.
4. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week of Physics — preview that next unit's forces will explain WHAT CAUSES acceleration.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to work through the two calculations (final velocity, then displacement) as fully separate steps, checking each before moving to the next
Ready for more: ask them to predict what would happen to the displacement if the acceleration doubled but time stayed the same, without recalculating first
This is a good checkpoint to note which part of the kinematics chain (distance/displacement, velocity, acceleration, or the equations) needs the most re-teaching
teacherGuide.answerKey: Final velocity: v = 6 + 5(4) = 26 m/s. Displacement: d = 6(4) + ½(5)(4²) = 24 + 40 = 64 meters. The three quantities are connected: velocity is the rate of change of position (displacement over time), and acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time — each builds on the one before it.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates NGSS HS-PS2-1's kinematic foundation before the unit moves to Newton's laws of motion (forces), matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.
